2027-05-26.title: Saint Philip Neri, Priest
readings: Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord
Show us, O Lord, the light of your kindness
The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many
2027-05-26.alt: Memorial. Wednesday of the Eighth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). The weekday readings are given here (first reading in NRSV numbering); the proper first reading of the memorial, Philippians 4:4–9, “Rejoice in the Lord always,” may be used instead. St Philip Neri, the Apostle of Rome, founded the Congregation of the Oratory. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-05-26.verse: For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
theo: The first reading is a prayer, one of the most fervent in the Wisdom books. Ben Sira's people are small and pressed on every side by powerful nations, and he cries out: “Have mercy upon us, O God of all, and put all the nations in fear of you.” But his deepest wish is not revenge. It is that the nations should come to know the true God: “As you have used us to show your holiness to them, so use them to show your glory to us. Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord.” Israel's suffering and Israel's rescue are meant to become a lesson for the whole world. Then the prayer grows tender: “Gather all the tribes of Jacob,” “Have mercy, O Lord, on the people called by your name, on Israel, whom you have named your firstborn,” “Have pity on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem.” And he ends with a line that the Church can pray at every Mass: “Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servants, according to your goodwill toward your people, and all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the God of the ages.” The Psalm, from a time of national disaster, prays in the same spirit: “Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name's sake.”

In the Gospel Jesus is walking ahead of his disciples on the road up to Jerusalem, and “they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid.” For the third time he tells them plainly what will happen: he will be handed over, condemned, mocked, flogged and killed, “and after three days he will rise again.” And at that very moment James and John come with a request: “Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.” They are thinking of thrones; he is thinking of a cross. “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink?” They answer bravely, “We are able,” and in time they will: James will be the first of the Twelve to die for Christ. The other ten are angry, perhaps because they wanted the same seats. So Jesus gathers them all and turns the world upside down: among the nations, rulers “lord it over them,” “but it is not so among you; but whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you must be slave of all. For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.” St Philip Neri, whom we remember today, could have had honours in the Rome of the popes. He refused the cardinal's hat more than once. He spent his life hearing confessions, visiting the sick in the hospitals, walking with young men from church to church, and making people laugh so that pride would have no room. He showed that the greatness Jesus speaks of can be joyful.
outline: Ask: if Jesus asked you today, “What do you want me to do for you?”, what would you say?
Point 1 · That all may know you
Ben Sira prays that God's people may become a light for the nations.
Point 2 · The cup and the thrones
James and John ask for glory; Jesus offers a share in his cup.
Point 3 · Not to be served but to serve
Greatness turned upside down, lived with joy by St Philip Neri.
“The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
live: Pray today for one country where Christ is not yet known, that its people may come to know the true God.
Do one humble task at home or at work today that nobody else wants to do, and do it cheerfully.
saints: Born in Florence, he came to Rome as a young man and lived for years as a layman, praying in the catacombs and caring for pilgrims and the sick. At Pentecost 1544, according to his own account, he felt the love of the Holy Spirit enter his heart like a ball of fire. Ordained priest in 1551, he gathered people for prayer, Scripture, music and conversation in a room above the church, the Oratory, from which the Congregation of the Oratory was born (approved 1575). Known for his humour, his long hours in the confessional and his care for the young, he is called the Apostle of Rome. He died on 26 May 1595 and was canonised in 1622.
2027-05-26.prayer: O God, who never cease to bestow the glory of holiness on the faithful servants you raise up for yourself, graciously grant that the Holy Spirit may kindle in us that fire with which he wonderfully filled the heart of Saint Philip Neri. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve. Deliver us from the wish for the first seats, and give us joy in the lowest place, so that all the earth may know that you are Lord. Amen.
altar: The cup Jesus asked James and John about is the cup he lifts at every Mass: “This is the cup of my Blood, the Blood of the new and eternal covenant, which will be poured out for you and for many.” Here the Son of Man still serves us, giving his life as a ransom, and those who drink from this cup are sent out to serve as he did.

quick: Ben Sira prays that God would gather his people and show his glory, so that all nations may know there is no God but the Lord.
James and John ask for the best seats in Christ's glory; Jesus asks if they can drink his cup.
Whoever wishes to be great must be a servant, for the Son of Man came to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.
2027-05-26.action: Do one humble task today that nobody else wants to do, cheerfully and without mentioning it.
2027-05-26.question: Am I looking for the first seat, or for the chance to serve?
kidsaint: Philip lived in Rome a long time ago and he was full of joy. He loved to tell jokes, play with children and sing. Sometimes he did funny things on purpose, like shaving only half his beard, so that people would laugh at him and he would not become proud. He looked after poor people and sick people, and he listened to people's confessions for hours. Children loved him. He used to tell them: be good, if you can! Lesson: being holy does not mean being sad; Jesus wants us to serve others with a happy heart.

family.explain: Two of Jesus' friends, James and John, asked him: when you are king, can we sit in the best chairs beside you? Jesus said: in my kingdom the greatest person is the one who serves others. I did not come to be served, but to serve. St Philip Neri lived like that: he helped the poor and sick, and he did it with a big smile.
family.intention: We pray for people who serve in our parish, and for those in hospitals who need someone to visit them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family serves everyone else the most? How can we help that person today?”

illus: A story is told of St Philip Neri and a woman who loved to gossip. She came to confession and he gave her a strange penance: take a chicken, pluck its feathers as you walk through the streets, and come back to me. She did it. Then he said: now go back and pick up every feather. She cried that it was impossible, the wind had carried them everywhere. Exactly, said Philip; so it is with the words you have spoken about others. (A traditional story, told in many forms.) Serving others begins with how we speak of them.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve. Fill us with the joy of the Holy Spirit, as you filled St Philip Neri, and teach us to serve. Amen.
share: Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord (Sirach 36:5). Does my life help anyone come to know God?
Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left (Mark 10:37). In what ways do I still look for honour and the first place?
Whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant (Mark 10:43). Whom could I serve this week, and how?
pm.resp: Show us, O Lord, the light of your kindness.
interc: For the Pope, the bishops and all who hold authority in the Church, that they may lead as servants.
For rulers and leaders of nations, that they may not lord it over their people.
For the Congregation of the Oratory and all who work with young people, through the prayers of St Philip Neri.
For the sick in hospitals and the lonely, that someone may visit them with joy.
For our group, that we may seek the lowest place and serve one another gladly.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave his life as a ransom for many. Give us his spirit of service, and the joy that filled St Philip Neri. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira prays for his small, suffering people, and his prayer is wider than his own nation. As you have used us to show your holiness to them, he prays, so use them to show your glory to us. Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord (Sirach 36:4–5). He wants the whole world to know the true God. That is still the prayer of the Church: that all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord.

In the Gospel Jesus is walking ahead on the road to Jerusalem. He tells the Twelve for the third time that he will suffer, die and rise. And right then James and John come and ask for the best seats: one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory (Mark 10:37). We smile at them. But how often we do the same: we follow Jesus, and quietly we hope for a little honour, a good name, a front seat.

Jesus answers gently: are you able to drink the cup that I drink? The cup is his suffering, his self-giving. Then he calls all twelve together and says: whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant. For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Mark 10:43, 45). In his kingdom, the chair of honour is a servant's stool.

St Philip Neri understood this. In Rome, a city full of honours and titles, he refused to become a cardinal. He spent his days in the confessional, in the hospitals, with poor young men. And he did it with joy, with jokes, with music. He showed that serving is not a sad duty; it is the joy of the Holy Spirit. Let us ask for that joy today, and look for one small chance to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, two of Jesus' friends wanted the best chairs, right next to Jesus! Jesus said: in my kingdom the most important person is the one who helps others. St Philip Neri was like that. He helped poor people and sick people, and he was always laughing and joking. Today, can you help someone at home, and do it with a big smile, like St Philip?

intro: Theme: “The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
A prayer that all nations may know God, a request for thrones, and a Master who serves.

sub: Hear the prayer of your servants.
q: Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servants, according to your goodwill toward your people, and all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the God of the ages.
And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for one nation or people who do not yet know Christ.

q: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name's sake.
But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
points.apply: When you receive Holy Communion this week, tell the Lord: I am willing to share your cup, give me strength.

points.h: Not to be served but to serve
sub: Rulers who lord it over others.
q: Do not exalt yourself, or you may fall and bring dishonor upon yourself.
But it is not so among you; but whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant,
points.apply: Each day this week do one hidden act of service with joy, as St Philip Neri would.

concl: Ben Sira prays that God's people may make God known to the nations.
Jesus shows how: not by thrones, but by the cup of self-giving and the joy of service.
2027-05-26.resolve: Look each day this week for the lowest place, and take it gladly.
